notes: Best-per-label pick across: access barriers→v05_faithful_paraphrase(100%), cost concerns→v05_faithful_paraphrase(100%), provider trust→v05_faithful_paraphrase(100%), wait times→v05_faithful_paraphrase(100%)

codes.name: access barriers
codes.definition: Structural obstacles that prevent a patient from accessing care, including physical distance, transportation issues, scheduling challenges, language barriers, and paperwork hurdles.
codes.clarification: Consider any factor that impedes a patient's ability to reach or book care, such as lack of proximity to a clinic, transportation constraints, or difficulties navigating the system.
codes.negative_clarification: Exclude price concerns, which are addressed under "cost concerns", even though both can prevent patients from receiving care.

positive_examples.text: The nearest clinic is two bus transfers away and I have to take a full day off work to get there.
positive_examples.why: Physical distance and transportation issues create a significant barrier to accessing care.

negative_examples.text: I saw the doctor, but the copay was more than I could afford, leaving me with a financial burden.
negative_examples.why: The obstacle here is the high cost of care, which prevents me from affording it.

codes.name: cost concerns
codes.definition: Worry about the monetary price of care — bills, copays, premiums, or fear of debt that may prevent patients from accessing care.
codes.clarification: Include any mention of affordability, insurance not covering enough, or skipping care due to financial constraints.
codes.negative_clarification: Exclude physical barriers to care, such as access barriers, which can also prevent patients from receiving care.

positive_examples.text: I skipped the follow-up appointment because I couldn't afford another $200 visit, leaving me with a significant financial burden.
positive_examples.why: Care was forgone specifically due to its high cost.

negative_examples.text: I waited for three months to get an appointment, which was frustrating but not directly related to the cost of care.
negative_examples.why: This is a scheduling delay, with no mention of financial constraints.

codes.name: provider trust
codes.definition: The patient's confidence in, or distrust of, their clinician or the health system, which can impact their willingness to seek and receive care.
codes.clarification: Consider feelings of being heard or dismissed, doubting a diagnosis, or relying on a provider's judgment.
codes.negative_clarification: Exclude general satisfaction with logistics like cost or wait times, as this is about the relationship and credibility of the provider.

positive_examples.text: My doctor never listens to me, so I've stopped trusting their advice and have started ignoring it.
positive_examples.why: Expresses distrust in the provider relationship due to a lack of communication.

negative_examples.text: The waiting room was crowded, but that didn't affect my trust in the provider or the care I received.
negative_examples.why: A logistics complaint (wait times), not about trust in the provider.

codes.name: wait times
codes.definition: Delay between seeking care and receiving it — appointment lead time or time spent waiting on the day.
codes.clarification: Include long lead times for appointments and long in-clinic waits, assuming care is reachable but slow.
codes.negative_clarification: Exclude situations where patients are unable to access care due to physical barriers, such as lack of proximity to a clinic or transportation issues.

positive_examples.text: The first available appointment was four months out, which added significant stress to my already busy schedule.
positive_examples.why: A direct delay in receiving care caused by an extended wait time.

negative_examples.text: There's no specialist within a hundred miles of me, making it difficult for me to access the care I need.
negative_examples.why: Care is unreachable due to physical distance, not just delayed.
